source.title: Evaluating Synthetic Activations composed of SAE Latents in GPT-2
source.authors: Giorgi Giglemiani; N. Petrova; Chatrik Singh Mangat; Jett Janiak; S. Heimersheim

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests SAE-latent compositions in GPT2-small, extending evidence about feature representations and superposition-related behavior from toy models to an LLM setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports perturbation outcomes for real, random, synthetic, and SAE-reconstructed activations, plus measured properties of SAE latents in model activations. Values used to select latent sparsity or cosine similarity are not recorded as results unless they are reported as outcomes. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: In GPT2-small layer 1, the study builds activations from SAE latents and from SAE reconstructions and compares their perturbation behaviour with real activations. It asks whether the model treats SAE latents as its units, and whether independent 'bags' of them suffice. That bears on V5's completeness and unit claim by a method different from the original's.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add three points: perturbing toward SAE-latent synthetic activations moves output more than toward random points, suggesting latents carry model-relevant information. SAE reconstructions behave almost like real activations, so the gaps come from the construction heuristics, not reconstruction error. The missing plateaus suggest further latent properties matter.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs synthetic GPT2-small activations from SAE latents and measures downstream perturbation sensitivity and plateaus; it does not use the original toy-model training or feature-interference recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on whether latent sparsity and cosine-similarity relationships are controlled, and on fixed versus relative perturbation step size. The gap between synthetic-baseline and synthetic-structured narrows under relative step size. The study uses one GPT2-small layer and the final token position.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT2-small is more sensitive to perturbations toward real activations than toward Gaussian-matched random points, and real activations sit on flatter plateaus. This is read as error correction for computation in superposition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Real LLM activations show noise-robust plateaus and directional sensitivity not shown by distribution-matched random points.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Attributing Model Behavior at Scale at NeurIPS 2024
record.problems: Evidence is limited to GPT2-small, one layer, and the final token position. The synthetic-activation construction uses heuristics and information from a base activation; the paper notes it does not match the cosine-similarity distribution closely and leaves co-occurrence and other latent relationships unmodeled. The authors note variability in perturbation curves and possible limitations of the MS metric. Plateau distributions are shown only in figures and lack reported numeric summaries.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity or importance as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Does not test whether features spread across neurons or whether an SAE recovers true features; it uses a pretrained SAE throughout.
Stability or canonicity across SAEs, seeds, layers or models; only one layer, one SAE family, last token.

missing.what: SAE-reconstruction relative-step MS statistics: mean 53.34, sd 8.39, KS 0.11 (random KS 0.61).
Absolute-step MS statistics for synthetic-random (51.30, KS 0.39) and structured without cosine similarity (50.17, KS 0.31).
Check that using a different real activation's information for construction does not change results.

record.verdict_notes: Workshop paper, one layer and one SAE. The reader's V4 links were dropped because neither the descriptive SAE statistics nor reconstruction fidelity test whether features are spread across neurons or are recoverable. The 'challenges' label on plateaus was downgraded to limits_scope: the failure is of the authors' construction heuristics, while reconstructions keep plateaus. Tranche changed to T2 (different method, same question in an LLM).

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-count-versus-dimension sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry of toy-model superposition is tested.
Does not test whether feature importance or capacity competition causes dedicated versus shared dimensions or neuron polysemanticity.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE-latent compositions and reconstruction behavior in GPT2-small, not feature spread across neurons, other models or layers, or general SAE recovery quality.
Tests whether constructed combinations of SAE latents reproduce selected activation behaviors. Does not establish whether SAE features are stable or canonical across contexts, models, or methods.
Uses latent directions and cosine similarity but does not test whether model features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relationships.condition: Synthetic activations built from independently chosen SAE latents (bag of latents / sparsity-matched), directional sensitivity
